metrics.label: Population
metrics.description: Resident population.
metrics.method: WorldPop 2020 pixels summed per hex, rescaled so every district (LKA) / county (USA) matches the official 2023 estimate.

metrics.label: Land area
metrics.description: Land area inside the country boundary.
metrics.method: Sum of raster-pixel areas whose centres fall inside the admin boundaries.

metrics.label: UNESCO World Heritage Sites
metrics.description: UNESCO World Heritage Sites (cultural, natural and mixed) located in the country.
metrics.method: Wikidata items with P1435 = Q9259 (non-deprecated, no end date) and P17 = country, grouped by the numeric part of the World Heritage Site id (P757; '72bis'/'72ter' -> 72); component items without an id are merged into a site within 3 km. The representative item is the member with the most Wikipedia sitelinks that has a coordinate inside the country grid (coordinates are tried in turn: grid cell, snap within 6 H3 rings, else nearest land hex within 250 km). For natural and mixed sites the coordinate is checked against the site's WDPA 'World Heritage Site (natural or mixed)' polygon (matched by name): a coordinate outside the country (the Yukon point of Kluane / Wrangell-St. Elias, the open-ocean point of Papahanaumokuakea) or more than 2 km outside the polygon (Sinharaja, whose Wikidata point is ~20 km SW of the reserve) is replaced by a representative point of polygon ∩ country (original kept in orig_lat/orig_lon). Sites whose coordinates are all outside the 50 states + DC (US territories, Mexico-only El Camino Real de Tierra Adentro, foreign components of transnational sites) are dropped. kind from the selection criteria (P2614): (i)-(vi) cultural, (vii)-(x) natural, both mixed. inscribed = earliest P580 start time of the designation (year of the original inscription). whs_ref keeps the raw P757 ids; a 'bis'/'ter' suffix (extended_or_modified) marks a later extension or boundary change, so the national component of a transnational site can be younger than `inscribed` (e.g. Moravian Church Settlements, 1468bis).

metrics.label: National park visitors
metrics.description: Annual visitors to national parks (USA: recreation visits; Sri Lanka: ticketed local + foreign visitors).
metrics.method: USA: NPS IRMA Stats Annual Park Ranking Report, calendar year 2025, Recreation Visits, Park Type = National Park (64 units); National Park of American Samoa and Virgin Islands NP (territories) are dropped, leaving 62 parks in the 50 states. Coordinates and area (P2046) from the Wikidata item of each park (instance of Q34918903, matched on normalised names: 'NP' -> National Park, 'NP & PRES' -> National Park and Preserve). Sri Lanka: SLTDA Year in Review 2025 Table 19 (Department of Wildlife Conservation), local + foreign visitors per park in 2025. Of its 23 rows, 'Eth Athuru Sevana' (the Udawalawe Elephant Transit Home, a rehabilitation facility) and 'Mirissa' (whale-watching tickets, not an area) are excluded, leaving 21 national parks, marine parks and sanctuaries (2,212,802 of the 2,604,243 visitors). 'Samanala Adaviya' is read as the Peak Wilderness Sanctuary and 'Bareef - Kalpitiya' as the Bar Reef Marine Sanctuary; Kalawewa and Girithale are located at the Kala Wewa and Giritale reservoirs (Wikidata). Coordinates from Wikidata; area_km2 from the WDPA polygon (GIS area) where the park is in WDPA, else Wikidata. US park coordinates more than 5 km outside the park's WDPA polygon (designation 'National Park', exact name match) are moved to a point inside it (Channel Islands: the Wikidata point is in the sea between the islands); original kept in orig_lat/orig_lon. Definitions differ: NPS counts recreation visits (person-entries, estimated from traffic counts for most parks); DWC counts tickets sold.

metrics.label: Museums
metrics.description: Museums with coordinates documented in Wikidata (count of points).
metrics.method: Wikidata items instance of museum (Q33506) or any subclass (art, history, science, house museums...), country P17 = Sri Lanka / United States, with coordinates; items with a dissolution (P576) or closure (P3999) date are dropped, one row per item (first coordinate). Items whose only museum-subclass types are visitor / nature / interpretation centres, heritage railways, film archives, cinematheques or virtual museums are dropped, as are points that do not snap to the country grid (US territories). Duplicate items for one institution are merged (same normalised name within 2 km, or the same coordinate with one name containing the other, e.g. a museum and its 'Main Building' item), keeping the item with most sitelinks. kind = the shortest English label among the item's museum-subclass P31 types other than plain 'museum' (else 'museum'). Coverage reflects Wikidata completeness, not an official museum census (the US IMLS universe lists far more institutions).

metrics.label: Protected area
metrics.description: Share of the hex area covered by designated protected areas (any IUCN category).
metrics.method: Union of WDPCA polygons with status Designated / Inscribed / Established, excluding UNESCO-MAB Biosphere Reserves (Protected Planet convention) and Proposed sites; all IUCN categories incl. 'Not Reported'. Coverage = share of the hex's H3 child-cell centres (res+3 = 343 points per hex for Sri Lanka, res+2 = 49 for the USA) that fall inside any polygon (shapely STRtree). Computed for every grid hex (land and coastal water, 0 where none); marine protected areas count in water hexes. Sri Lanka's polygons are full resolution; US polygons were generalised server-side (maxAllowableOffset 0.005 deg ~ 500 m). WDPA point-only records (no boundary) are not counted.

metrics.label: Strictly protected area (IUCN Ia-IV)
metrics.description: Share of the hex area covered by protected areas in IUCN categories Ia, Ib, II, III or IV.
metrics.method: As protected_pct, restricted to polygons whose iucn_cat is Ia, Ib, II, III or IV (strict reserves, wilderness, national parks, natural monuments, habitat/species management areas). Categories are as reported to WDPA: Sri Lanka reports most Forest Department Reserved Forests as Ib, so its strict share is close to its total share; most US conservation easements and state lands are V or 'Not Assigned'.

metrics.label: Protected area
metrics.description: Area of the hex (land or sea) inside designated protected areas.
metrics.method: protected_pct / 100 x H3 cell area. Overlapping designations are counted once.

metrics.label: Tourist accommodation rooms
metrics.description: Rooms in SLTDA-registered tourist accommodation (hotels, boutique villas, guest houses, bungalows, homestays, rented apartments...).
metrics.method: SLTDA Year in Review 2025 Table 12 'Total rooms by districts, 2025' (p. 36), transcribed; district names matched to COD-AB pcodes (Moneragala -> Monaragala, Rathnapura -> Ratnapura). Allocated to hexes by built-up land cover (fallback land area).

metrics.label: GDP (Gold)
metrics.description: Gross domestic product at current prices, US dollars.
metrics.method: USA: BEA CAGDP2, year 2024, current dollars (thousands x 1,000). Lines: total = 1; agriculture = 3 (NAICS 11); industry = 6 + 10 + 11 + 13 + 25 (mining, utilities, construction, durable + nondurable manufacturing); services = total - agriculture - industry (includes government, line 83); manufacturing = 13 + 25 (= line 12); finance = 51 + 56 + 60 (finance & insurance; real estate & rental/leasing; professional, scientific & technical services). Suppressed '(D)' county cells (18,737 in 2024; BEA suppresses complementary cells, so no identity has a single unknown) are estimated for the 20 leaf industries that partition line 2 (private industries) by multi-margin iterative proportional fitting within each state, seeded with ACS 2024 5-year C24030 employment of the matching industry (+1). Margins: every disclosed county aggregate (lines 2, 91, 92, 87, 12, 50, 59, 68, 75, 88, 89, 90, minus its disclosed leaves) and every state leaf total (state value minus disclosed counties). Disclosed county aggregates are reproduced to within BEA's own $1-4 thousand rounding except a handful of counties (all < 0.1 %) and state industry totals to within 0.02 % (exact figures in report.json); national sector totals equal the sum of BEA state rows. BEA combination areas (23 Virginia county + independent-city combinations, Maui + Kalawao) are split to Census 2023 counties pro rata to 2023 population (Census PEP vintage 2023). Totals are the sum of the 50 states + DC; BEA's US row also includes overseas federal government activity (the whole ~0.55 % gap is in line 83, government). Allocation to hexes: population-weighted within each county. gdp_usd = line 1 (all-industry total). | Sri Lanka: Province level (2024, current market prices, Rs mn): national GVA by sector from DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 10.2 (agriculture = A&F&F; industry = manufacturing, mining & other industries + construction; services = the seven service activities). Provincial shares of each sector: the shares quoted from the CBSL PGDP 2024 release are used directly (agriculture: NW 20.0, C 13.9, S 11.8; industry: W 47.6, NW 12.0, C 9.6; services: W 44.5, C 10.7, NW 10.1 %); Western agriculture is the residual that makes Western's GVA share equal its published GDP share (42.4 %); the remaining share of each sector is split among the other provinces in proportion to their 2020 CBSL provincial GVA in that sector (DOSE v2.9, 2010-base series). Net taxes on products (taxes 2,641,646 - subsidies 39,873) are allocated pro rata to provincial GVA. Check: the derived NW and Central GDP shares reproduce the published 11.5 % and 10.7 % (see report.json). District level: each provincial sector total is split over its districts in proportion to LFS 2024 Table 13 employment in that sector (agriculture) or that employment x HIES 2019 mean monthly household income of the district (industry, services; a relative productivity proxy, because LFS counts workers where they live). Net taxes follow district GVA. Districts sum exactly to provinces and the national total equals DCS GDP. Converted at the World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF 2024 average rate. Allocation to hexes: population-weighted within each district. gdp_usd = GVA at basic prices + net taxes on products = GDP at market prices. Note: US county GDP is industry value added (taxes on production are inside industry value added), so both are GDP at market prices.

metrics.label: Median household income
metrics.description: Median annual household income, current US dollars of the survey year.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 2020-2024 5-year B19013_E001 (median household income in the past 12 months, 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars), county. | Sri Lanka: HIES 2019 Final Results Table 01, district MEDIAN monthly household income (Rs, all income incl. in-kind and imputed rent of owner-occupied housing) x 12, converted at the World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF 2019 average rate. Different survey years (2019 vs 2024 $) and income concepts: compare levels with care (no PPP adjustment applied).

metrics.label: Poverty rate
metrics.description: Share of people living below the national official poverty line.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 5-year B17001_E002 / B17001_E001 x 100 (people below the Census Bureau's income-based official poverty thresholds, by family size/composition; universe = people for whom poverty status is determined). | Sri Lanka: DCS Poverty Indicators 2019 Table 04 headcount index under the UPDATED official poverty line (consumption-based, Rs 6,966 per person per month in 2019 = about US$39 at the 2019 PA.NUS.FCRF rate; cost-of-basic-needs line anchored at 2,030 kcal per person per day). The two national lines are very different absolute standards (the Sri Lankan line is far below the US thresholds), so rates are comparable only within each country.

metrics.label: People in poverty
metrics.description: Number of people below the national official poverty line.
metrics.method: USA: ACS 5-year B17001_E002. | Sri Lanka: Poverty Indicators 2019 Table 04, number of poor people under the updated official poverty line. Same definitional caveats as poverty_rate.

metrics.label: Relative Wealth Index
metrics.description: Meta Relative Wealth Index: predicted asset-based wealth relative to the rest of Sri Lanka (unitless relative scale; higher = wealthier; tile statistics in report.json).
metrics.method: Unweighted mean of the RWI values of the 2.4 km Bing quadkey tiles whose centre falls in each H3 res-6 land cell (tiles centred in a sea cell are snapped to the nearest adjacent land cell). Land cells with no tile take the mean of the original cell values within 1 ring, then 2 rings; cells still without a value (uninhabited parts of Yala and Wilpattu national parks, where Meta publishes no tile) stay empty. No US equivalent (the RWI covers low- and middle-income countries only).

metrics.label: Agriculture, forestry & fishing GVA (Food)
metrics.description: Gross value added of agriculture, forestry and fishing (ISIC A / NAICS 11), current US dollars.
metrics.method: USA 2025: BEA SAGDP2 state GDP of agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (line 3), current dollars, split to counties by each county's share of its state's NAICS 11 GDP in BEA CAGDP2 2024 (line 3; published county values, the latest county year). Counties sum exactly to the BEA state rows (50 states + DC). Proxy used only where BEA publishes no single-county value: SAGDP2 line 4 (farms) shared by the county's 2022 Census of Agriculture market value of products sold (Table 1; sales-share caveats as for ag_sales_usd) + line 5 (forestry, fishing, and related activities) shared by ACS 2020-2024 5-year employment in agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting (C24030 lines 4 + 31, place of residence). (a) CAGDP2 cells suppressed '(D)': the state row minus the disclosed units is shared among the suppressed units in proportion to the proxy; (b) BEA combination areas (Virginia county + independent cities, Maui + Kalawao) are split to their member counties in proportion to the proxy. Hex allocation: cropland weight. | Sri Lanka 2024: national GVA of the 17 agriculture, forestry & fishing activities at current prices (DCS revised QGDP 2024, Table 21, four quarters summed; Rs 2,520,119 mn, vs Rs 2,481,487 mn in the earlier Statistical Abstract 2025 vintage) is spread over the 25 districts activity by activity, in proportion to a physical indicator of each activity. Activity -> district indicator: rice -> paddy production Maha 2023/24 + Yala 2024 (Abstract 5.20); cereals except rice -> highland cereal extent (kurakkan, maize, sorghum, meneri), Maha 2023/24 + Yala 2024 (5.17); vegetables and sugar cane/tobacco/other non-perennials -> total highland-crop extent of the same seasons (5.17); tea, rubber, coconut -> 2014 census extents (5.2); fruits -> 2014 extent of systematic fruit cultivation (EC 2013/14 Table 23); coffee/cocoa -> 2014 cocoa + coffee extent (Table 22); spices -> 2014 cinnamon, pepper, cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, betel and arecanut extent (Table 22) + 2023/24 ginger and turmeric extent (5.17); animal production -> mean of the district shares of cattle + buffalo and of poultry (2014, Tables 28 and 30; equal weights are an assumption); other perennials, plant propagation, support activities and forestry & logging -> total agricultural land 2014 (Table 2); marine fishing -> marine fish production 2024 (5.34, fisheries districts mapped to administrative districts: Negombo -> Gampaha, Chilaw + Puttalam -> Puttalam, Tangalle -> Hambantota, Kalmunai -> Ampara; mapping verified against MoF Table 4.3 for 2023); fresh-water fishing -> inland & aquaculture production 2023 (MoF Table 4.3). Provincial calibration: the district index is rescaled so that the province totals equal the agriculture shares of the CBSL Provincial GDP 2024 release: North Western 20.0 %, Central 13.9 %, Southern 11.8 % (quoted), Western derived as (42.4 % x GVA - 47.6 % x industry - 44.5 % x services) / agriculture with the DCS Abstract Table 10.2 sector values (i.e. assuming net product taxes are distributed like GVA) = 11.86 %, capped at 11.7 % because the release ranks Southern (11.8 %) third (the residual carries ~1 pp rounding error from shares quoted to 0.1 pp); the remaining share is split among the other five provinces in proportion to their index totals. Within a province districts keep their index proportions. Converted at the World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF 2024 average rate. Hex allocation: cropland weight.

metrics.label: Tree & plantation crop share of agricultural land
metrics.description: Share of agricultural land under perennial tree / plantation crops (drives Plantation districts).
metrics.method: USA: 2022 Census of Agriculture land in orchards (Table 30: fruit and nut trees, citrus, vineyards, bearing + non-bearing acres) / total cropland (Table 1) x 100 - orchards are part of cropland, so the share is <= 100. Withheld '(D)' acres are filled per state from the state total minus disclosed counties: cropland shared by farms with cropland; orchards shared by the county's 2017 orchard acres (Table 30, else farms x the state median acres per orchard farm) and capped at the county's cropland. Alaska / Connecticut are split as for ag_sales_usd (both acreages with the same weights). Counties with less than 200 acres of cropland: no value. | Sri Lanka: (tea + rubber + coconut extent) / total agricultural land of small holdings and estates x 100, Economic Census 2013/14 (tea and coconut: DCS Abstract 2025 Table 5.2 in hectares; rubber: EC 2013/14 Table 6.3.1; land: EC 2013/14 Table 2; acres converted at 0.404686 ha/acre). Definitional difference: the US denominator is cropland (excludes permanent pasture and woodland), the Sri Lankan one all agricultural land of holdings (incl. home gardens); the US numerator excludes berries, nurseries and Christmas trees.

metrics.label: Paddy production
metrics.description: Paddy (unmilled rice) production of the 2024 cultivation year.
metrics.method: DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 5.20 (Paddy Statistics, crop-cutting survey), production '000 MT of Maha 2023/24 + Yala 2024 x 1,000. Jaffna has no Yala cultivation (0). National total checked against Table 5.19 (4,698,454 t).

metrics.label: Tea extent
metrics.description: Cultivated extent of tea (small holdings + estates).
metrics.method: DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 5.2, 2014 column (Economic Census 2013/14, agricultural activities). District tea production is not published (Tea Board production is by elevation), so extent is used. '..' read as 0.

metrics.label: Rubber extent
metrics.description: Cultivated extent of rubber.
metrics.method: Economic Census 2013/14 report Table 6.3.1 (extent under rubber by district, acres x 0.404686). Abstract 2025 Table 5.2 carries the same census figures in hectares but prints '..' for Kurunegala (8,015 acres = 3,244 ha in the census report) although its national total (112,141 ha) includes it; the district sum is checked against that total. Districts without rubber are absent from the census table (0).

metrics.label: Coconut extent
metrics.description: Cultivated extent of coconut.
metrics.method: DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 5.2, 2014 column (Economic Census 2013/14; systematic cultivation incl. estimated extent of scattered trees).

metrics.label: Highland (other field) crop extent
metrics.description: Seasonal extent cultivated with highland crops (cereals other than rice, pulses, oilseeds, roots & tubers, onions, chillies, ginger, turmeric).
metrics.method: DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 5.17, sum of all crop columns for Maha 2023/24 and Yala 2024 (gross seasonal extent: land cropped in both seasons counts twice). '..' read as 0.

metrics.label: Marine fish production / commercial landings
metrics.description: Marine fish catch landed, metric tonnes (live weight).
metrics.method: Sri Lanka: DCS Statistical Abstract 2025 Table 5.34, marine fish production 2024 by the 15 fisheries districts (coastal + offshore/multi-day; Ministry of Fisheries estimates), mapped to administrative districts (Negombo -> Gampaha, Chilaw + Puttalam -> Puttalam, Tangalle -> Hambantota, Kalmunai -> Ampara; others same name; the mapping reproduces MoF Table 4.3's 2023 administrative-district figures exactly). Inland districts 0. Comparable to the US commercial marine landings (state level). Hex allocation: coast weight.

metrics.label: Inland fisheries & aquaculture production
metrics.description: Inland capture fisheries and aquaculture production, metric tonnes.
metrics.method: Ministry of Fisheries 'Fisheries Statistics 2024' Table 4.3, inland & aquaculture production 2023 by administrative district (latest year with district detail; national 2024 total 102,330 t per Abstract 5.33). No comparable US series (FOSS has no aquaculture and Great Lakes data end in 2018).

metrics.label: Tropical cyclone passes (1980-2026)
metrics.description: Number of distinct tropical cyclones whose track passed within 100 km of the hex centre at tropical-storm strength or more, 1980 season to the latest (provisional) 2026 track.
metrics.method: IBTrACS since1980 list: main, PROVISIONAL and US-PROVISIONAL tracks (spurs dropped), points filtered to a box 5 deg around the country.  Wind = USA_WIND (1-min sustained, JTWC/NHC/CPHC) if reported, else WMO_WIND (agency-specific averaging, e.g. IMD 3-min, RSMC Tokyo 10-min).  A track point qualifies if NATURE is not ET (extratropical) or DS (disturbance) - TS (tropical), SS (subtropical), MX and NR are kept - and its wind is >= 34 kt.  Points with no reported wind never qualify (IBTrACS NATURE 'TS' means 'Tropical', any intensity, so it is not used as a strength proxy).  Consecutive points of a storm (<= 6 h apart) are densified to <= 10 km steps (great-circle interpolation of position; wind interpolated linearly when both fixes report one, otherwise the half-segment next to the fix with a wind takes that wind) so fast storms are not missed between 3-hourly fixes.  Count = distinct SIDs with any qualifying point within 100 km.  Exposure frequency at a point (not additive across hexes). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Strongest cyclone wind nearby (1980-2026)
metrics.description: Highest maximum sustained wind (knots) of any qualifying tropical cyclone while its track was within 100 km of the hex centre.
metrics.method: Max of the (interpolated) track-point wind over the qualifying points counted in cyclone_tracks.  USA_WIND (1-min) preferred, WMO_WIND fallback.  0 = no qualifying pass. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: M5+ earthquakes within 100 km (1976-2025)
metrics.description: Number of magnitude >= 5.0 earthquakes with epicentre within 100 km of the hex centre, 1 Jan 1976 - 31 Dec 2025 (any depth).
metrics.method: USGS ComCat FDSN CSV (preferred magnitude 'mag', any magType; eventtype=earthquake), deduplicated by event id across overlapping search boxes.  Exposure frequency at a point (not additive). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Largest earthquake within 100 km (1976-2025)
metrics.description: Largest magnitude among the M5+ earthquakes within 100 km of the hex centre.
metrics.method: Max of ComCat preferred magnitude over events counted in quakes_m5.  0 = no M5+ event. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Tsunami runup observations within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Number of NOAA NCEI tsunami runup / tide-gauge observations located within 25 km of the hex centre since 1900.
metrics.method: HazEL runups API, boxes around each country (no country filter, so cross-border runups count). Kept: year >= 1900 and source event validity >= 3 (probable or definite tsunami; seiches, doubtful and erroneous events dropped).  Each runup record counts once (one tsunami usually produces several records along a coast). Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Tsunamis observed within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Number of distinct tsunamis (source events) with at least one NOAA NCEI runup / tide-gauge observation within 25 km of the hex centre since 1900.
metrics.method: Same runup records as tsunami_runups, counted by distinct tsunamiEventId instead of by record, so a heavily surveyed single event (e.g. the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami along Sri Lanka's coast) counts once.  A frequency measure, used in hazard_index. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Highest tsunami water height within 25 km (1900-2026)
metrics.description: Maximum tsunami water height (runup or tide-gauge amplitude, metres) among the observations counted in tsunami_runups.
metrics.method: Max of runupHt over the kept runup records; records without a height are counted but do not set the maximum.  0 = no observation with a height. Great-circle search around each hex centre (core.load_hexes lat/lon; land and water-ring hexes) using 3-D unit vectors in a scipy cKDTree.  Radius-based, so the value does not depend on hex size (LKA res-6 and USA res-5 tiles are comparable). 0 = no qualifying event.

metrics.label: Natural hazard index
metrics.description: Composite 0-100 exposure to tropical cyclones, strong earthquakes and tsunamis, on one scale for both countries (100 = most exposed).
metrics.method: Three event-frequency inputs: cyclone_tracks, quakes_m5 and tsunami_events (distinct tsunamis, not runup records).  For each input, a hex with 0 events scores 0; a hex with >= 1 event scores the mid-rank percentile of its value among all LAND hexes of BOTH countries (Sri Lanka res-6 + USA res-5 pooled) that have >= 1 event of that hazard: (n_below + 0.5 n_equal) / n_exposed.  Ranking among exposed hexes only keeps a single storm in 47 years from scoring like a hurricane coast just because most US hexes see none.  hazard_index = 100 x mean of the three scores, so a place exposed to only one hazard tops out near 33 and multi-hazard coasts (Hawaii, Alaska, California) score highest.  The reference distribution is pooled, so values are comparable between countries (inputs are radius counts, independent of hex size).  Each land hex counts once in the pool, so per km2 Sri Lanka's smaller res-6 tiles carry ~7x the weight of US res-5 tiles (Sri Lanka is ~5% of the pooled land hexes, but a larger share of the cyclone-exposed ones).  Floods, droughts, landslides, wildfire and tornadoes are not in this index (no consistent hex-level catalogue for both countries); see the admin tables for those.

Grouped by district (level1 code -> COD-AB pcode by name).  Allocated to hexes by population.

metrics.label: People affected by natural disasters (1990-2019)

metrics.method: Sum of 'afectados' (DesInventar 'Affected') over the same datacards as disaster_deaths.  Drought datacards contribute most of the total.  Allocated to hexes by population.

metrics.label: Houses destroyed by natural disasters (1990-2019)

metrics.method: Sum of 'vivdest' (Houses destroyed) over the same datacards as disaster_deaths.  Allocated to hexes by population.

metrics.label: Flood events (1990-2019)
metrics.description: Number of flood event-days recorded in the district, 1990-2019.
metrics.method: Event-days: distinct dates with at least one datacard in the district for FLOOD, FLASH FLOOD, URBAN FLOOD or CYCLONE & FLOOD (datacards of the same day at several GN / DS units, or of several types of the family, count once; a multi-day event reported on several dates counts once per date).  A district-level frequency: every hex in the district carries the district's count (intensive, land weight).

metrics.label: Landslide events (1990-2019)

metrics.method: As flood_events, for LANDSLIDE, EARTH SLIP, ROCK FALL and CUTTING FAILURE.

metrics.label: Drought events (1990-2019)

metrics.label: Cyclone events (1990-2019)

metrics.label: Power plant capacity
metrics.vintage: USA 2025; LKA 2023 (CEB plants) / GPPD v1.3.0, capacity year not stated (others)
metrics.description: Installed (nameplate) electric generating capacity of utility-scale power plants.
metrics.method: USA: EIA-860 2025 generator file, sheet 'Operable', summing nameplate MW of generators with status OP (operating) or SB (standby) per plant; generators out of service (OS/OA) excluded; plants in the 50 states + DC at EIA-860 plant coordinates. LKA: CEB-owned stations from CEB Annual Report 2023 Tables G1-G3 (Old+New Laxapana reported as one 153.8 MW station; the four Kelanitissa units KCCP 165 + KCCP2 157 + GT7 115 + Frame V GTs 80 = 517 MW combined into one point; Uma Oya 120 MW added from the same report, commissioned Apr 2024); other plants from WRI GPPD v1.3.0. GPPD coordinates more than 20 km from every Wikidata power station / dam of the same name are replaced by the Wikidata coordinate (Old Laxapana, Polpitiya, Samanala), and Inginiyagala, whose GPPD point duplicates Bowatenna Dam, is placed at the Gal Oya Dam. Three small legacy independent oil plants in GPPD (Asia Power 51 MW, Northern Power 36 MW, Lakdhanavi 24 MW) are dropped because the CEB Statistical Digest 2025 lists only 2 independent oil-fired stations (482 MW in 2024), which the 300 MW Yugadanavi plant already dominates. metrics.label: Electricity generation
metrics.description: Annual net electricity generation of each plant.

LKA: CEB-owned stations use reported 2023 net generation (CEB Annual Report 2023 Tables G1-G3); other plants use GPPD v1.3.0 'estimated_generation_gwh_2017' (modelled: CAPACITY-FACTOR-V1 / HYDRO-V1 / SOLAR-V1-NO-AGE), except that an estimate larger than the 2024 net generation of all IPP plants of that technology (CEB Statistical Digest 2025) is set to NaN: this drops Yugadanavi (GPPD 1,396 GWh vs 768 GWh for both IPP oil stations); the estimate is kept in column generation_gwh_gppd_estimate. USA: plants reported in EIA-923 without an operating/standby generator in EIA-860 are not mapped (count and GWh in the infra report). Columns generation_year and generation_basis record which applies.

metrics.label: Renewable power capacity

Ports with zero estimated cargo are dropped (Galle), as are PortWatch 'USA' ports that do not snap to the 50-states + DC grid (a mislabelled 'Sydney' at 46.2N 60.2W and the deep-water 'Offshore Oil Terminal 1' at 26.4N 90.8W). metrics.label: Military installations

metrics.label: Mean elevation

metrics.method: Copernicus GLO-90 DSM pixels assigned to the H3 hex whose boundary contains the pixel centre (H3 polygons rasterised on each DEM tile grid). Both countries use the native 3 arc-sec tiles (~90 m N-S; E-W spacing widens north of 50N following the GLO tiling: 4.5 arc-sec at 50-60N, 6 at 60-70N, 9 at 70-80N), so values are comparable between Sri Lanka and the US. Statistics use pixels with DEM != 0 (land and inland-water surfaces, which the DEM flattens; ocean is 0 m and absent tiles are sea); hexes without such pixels get 0 m and 0 deg. Means are weighted by pixel area. DSM heights include canopy/buildings, relative to the EGM2008 geoid; 90 m pixels smooth sharp summits, so hex maxima sit somewhat below surveyed peak heights. Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land inside a US border hex is included).

metrics.label: Land cover: Tree cover

metrics.method: Share of the hex's pixels in WorldCover class 10 (Tree cover). WorldCover pixels (Sri Lanka: all native 10 m pixels; USA: the COG's 4x internal overview, 1/3000 deg ~ 40 m, which was built with mode resampling, so scattered minority classes are under-represented: against native 10 m pixels around 80 random US land hexes (mostly rural), built-up was -11% relative (max 0.5 percentage points per hex), shrub/wetland/moss -1 to -2%, other classes within +-0.5%; in dense urban hexes built-up is instead over-represented by ~2-3 points (Manhattan, Silicon Valley). Sri Lankan shares (10 m) have no such bias) are assigned to the hex containing their centre (rasterised H3 polygons); fractions are over the whole hex area, so the 11 classes sum to 1. Open ocean (no-data 0 inside tiles, or no tile at all) is counted as water (class 80). Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land included); the *_km2 weights are in-country only.

metrics.method: Share of the hex's pixels in WorldCover class 50 (Built-up). WorldCover pixels (Sri Lanka: all native 10 m pixels; USA: the COG's 4x internal overview, 1/3000 deg ~ 40 m, which was built with mode resampling, so scattered minority classes are under-represented: against native 10 m pixels around 80 random US land hexes (mostly rural), built-up was -11% relative (max 0.5 percentage points per hex), shrub/wetland/moss -1 to -2%, other classes within +-0.5%; in dense urban hexes built-up is instead over-represented by ~2-3 points (Manhattan, Silicon Valley). Sri Lankan shares (10 m) have no such bias) are assigned to the hex containing their centre (rasterised H3 polygons); fractions are over the whole hex area, so the 11 classes sum to 1. Open ocean (no-data 0 inside tiles, or no tile at all) is counted as water (class 80). Border hexes are described as whole hexes (foreign land included); the *_km2 weights are in-country only.

metrics.label: Cropland area

metrics.method: Cropland area (km2) = share of the hex's in-country WorldCover pixels (centre inside the COD-AB / Census cartographic boundary union) in class 40 x core land_km2 of the hex (WorldPop pixel-area crosswalk). Border hexes therefore exclude Canadian/Mexican land; water-ring hexes with land_km2 = 0 get 0. Hexes with land_km2 > 0 but no in-country WorldCover pixel at the processing resolution fall back to the whole-hex non-water shares. metrics.label: Population density
metrics.description: People per km² of land.
metrics.method: pop / land_km2

metrics.label: GDP per capita
metrics.description: GDP per resident at current prices.
metrics.method: Tiles: gdp_usd ÷ residents (tiles with ≥ 50 residents; equal to the population-weighted value of the units the tile overlaps). Admin units: unit GDP ÷ unit population. gdp_usd of the county/district divided by its 2023 population used by the core grid (US Census PEP vintage 2023; Sri Lanka DCS mid-2023 estimates via COD-PS). USA: BEA county GDP is workplace-based, so commuter and resource hubs (Manhattan, DC, oil counties such as Loving County TX with 43 residents) are strongly inflated. Sri Lanka: provincial GDP is workplace-based, but the district split uses LFS employment by place of residence, so commuting into Colombo district is NOT captured (Colombo likely understated, Gampaha/Kalutara overstated).

metrics.label: Farmers (agriculture, forestry & fishery workers) (share)
metrics.description: Skilled agricultural, forestry & fishery workers and agricultural labourers.
metrics.method: cit_farmers / employed × 100. Sri Lanka LFS 2024 (DCS), household population aged 15+. District figures are LFS estimates (appendix Table 12/13) or estimates derived from province tables (14/15). Each district value is spread over the district's Census 2024 DS divisions in proportion to their census counts (DCS census data portal), and the census-DS values are then moved to the COD-AB DS divisions with a WorldPop 100 m population-weighted overlay. National totals are exact; where COD-AB and 2024 census boundaries differ, COD district sums deviate from the LFS district figures (up to 2.3%, Polonnaruwa). Occupation: province employment by ISCO-08 major group (LFS Table 14) split to district x industry by iterative proportional fitting (seed = district x ISIC-group employment x national occupation mix of each industry from ILOSTAT's 2024 LFS cross-tab; margins = Table 14 province totals and district x industry totals), then cut into classes with national ISCO-08 2-digit shares of LFS 2024 (ILOSTAT). Inside a district, DS employment is split into agriculture / industry / services with a seed of the census 2024 urban-population share of the DS (tot_Sec_Ur / tot_Sec) x the national LFS 2024 sector mix of urban and of rural (incl. estate) employment (ILOSTAT EMP_TEMP_SEX_ECO_GEO_NB_A: urban 4.0% agriculture vs rural 30.3%), raked to DS employment and to the district sector totals of Table 13; the district's industry (or class) mix within each sector then applies, so DS divisions with the same urban share in one district have the same composition. The census publishes no DS-level industry or occupation counts. Class mapping: ISCO-08 major group 6 (61-63 incl. ILO 'not classified' X, which belongs to group 6) + elementary workers (group 9) employed in agriculture, taken as ISCO 92 agricultural, forestry & fishery labourers, + the remaining ISCO 92 share of non-agricultural elementary workers (ILOSTAT 2024: 92 = 888.2k vs 843.0k elementary workers in agriculture).

The census publishes no DS-level industry or occupation counts. Class mapping: Proxy: ISCO-08 34 legal, social, cultural & related associate professionals (share of group 3: 342 sports & fitness, 343 artistic, cultural & culinary associates, but also 341 legal, social & religious associates).
